# LibRaw source dependency

Pinned upstream: [LibRaw 0.22.2](https://github.com/LibRaw/LibRaw/tree/b93f6e45c194f5df9b02a43b1af9a54b4f41f33f), commit `b93f6e45c194f5df9b02a43b1af9a54b4f41f33f`. `upstream/` contains original `src/`, `internal/`, `libraw/`, copyright, both license texts, README and source-list Makefile. No upstream files have been modified.

This project selects the LGPL 2.1 licensing option offered in upstream COPYRIGHT. Preserve `upstream/COPYRIGHT`, `LICENSE.LGPL`, `LICENSE.CDDL` and embedded source notices. The library's other embedded copyright notices remain in the original sources. This dependency is separate from recovered APK assets and application code.

`source-manifest.json` records source paths, SHA-256 and commit. `sources.cmake` copies the library source list from pinned `Makefile.am`; examples, benchmark programs, upstream build scripts and nested Git metadata are not run or included in the Android build. `tools/vendor_libraw.py` reproduces the copy from a clean matching checkout at `tools/.cache/libraw-0.22.2` and refuses changed destination files.

Android integration is in `native/raw-preview/`. Default import still extracts embedded JPEGs. The maintainer explicitly authorized optional sensor decoding, then selected a 10-bit working compromise: `unpack()` / `dcraw_process()` with camera white balance and no auto-brightening, balanced half-size/bilinear or full-size/AHD. Temporary 16-bit linear ProPhoto D65 RGB is quantized once through an sRGB-like transfer into three 10-bit channels packed in a 32-bit working word. The private original RAW is retained. Float sampling/adjustments and film/LUT lookups read this cache directly; the 8-bit PNG in the legacy source slot is a preview/target surface, never the precision source. Ordinary JPEG/PNG deliverables remain 8-bit.

`native/common/raw10.hpp` adapts the inverse of the pinned `LibRaw_constants::prophoto_rgb` matrix for model-input conversion. This is LibRaw's ProPhoto D65 basis, not an assertion that the cache is a standard ICC ProPhoto D50 file. Source/profile bytes, licensing and notices are unchanged. RAW film rendering currently uses the native CPU precision route; JPEG GLES remains unchanged. No optional SDK/OpenMP is added. Source compilation does not establish camera compatibility, colour accuracy, orientation, gradient quality, memory or performance on a physical phone. Targeted native precision and synthetic Bayer DNG checks, plus actual JNI import/rendering in an isolated Android emulator, passed after explicit maintainer authorization. No broad suite, physical-camera sample or performance benchmark was run.
